Chapter 6: Reaching for Dreams in a World That Doesn’t Wait.
Let’s be honest—sometimes, the hardest part of healing isn’t the pain itself. It’s daring to want more.
When you’ve spent years just trying to get by, the idea of reaching for a dream can feel almost reckless, can’t it? Like you’re tempting fate, asking for too much. But after so long just watching life from the sidelines, that pull—the hope for something better—it’s tough to ignore.
There was a time when her ambitions were small. They had to be. She needed the basics: a safe place to sleep, a steady paycheck, just a bit of peace. But as her confidence started to grow, her vision for life grew right along with it.
She began to imagine a future that wasn’t just about making it through the day, but about actually thriving. About doing work that meant something. Building relationships that felt real. Maybe—even finding a place to truly call home.
Of course, the world didn’t exactly stop to make space for her dreams. Bills still showed up. Setbacks popped up out of nowhere. And there were plenty of days when those old doubts whispered, “Who are you to ask for more?” But she kept going. One small step at a time.
She took a leap on a job that felt just out of reach—applying for a position that needed skills she wasn’t even sure she had. The interview? Nerve-wracking. Her hands shook, her voice wavered as she tried to sound like she belonged there. But the manager heard something in her story—a quiet determination, a willingness to learn. And she got the job.
That new job changed everything. Suddenly, work was more than just a paycheck—it was a place to test her limits. To see what she was truly capable of. There were mistakes, of course. Missed deadlines. Awkward conversations. Moments where she felt completely in over her head. But every single challenge became a chance to grow—to prove to herself she could handle more than she’d ever imagined.
Outside of work, she started nurturing her creative side. Writing, which had always been a private escape, turned into a way to process her experiences—and, eventually, to connect with others. She shared her stories, first with close friends, then with a bigger audience. And the response? Overwhelming. Messages poured in from people who saw themselves in her words—people who thanked her for saying what they couldn’t.
What she realized was, dreams don’t have to be huge to matter. Sometimes, the most important victories are the quiet ones—showing up, trying again, refusing to give up. For her, reaching for something more wasn’t just about ambition. It was a way to honor everything she’d survived, and everything she still hoped to become.
Most people don’t realize just how much courage it takes to want more—especially after a lifetime of being told to settle. But here’s the truth: every step you take toward a dream, no matter how small, is a step toward freedom.
